title: Alleged jihadist terrorist who created propaganda with AI arrested in Cornella de Llobregat

reading.body:
This is a case of a generative AI tool used to produce propaganda material, not a case of a model failing on its own terms. The AI component appears as one item in a wider enforcement action: a suspect is reported to have designed jihadist multimedia content with artificial intelligence tools while using encrypted social media and messaging apps to radicalise others. The technology sits inside a distribution and recruitment operation, and the reporting does not describe which tools were used, what they generated, or how the output performed.

The failure mode here is misuse by a person, not a system asserting something false, not an automated decision made without a human check, and not a model deployed outside its intended conditions. Nothing in the reports indicates that any AI provider was aware of the use or that a product malfunctioned. Catching this kind of use would not come from model evaluation or output review, because the content was circulated in encrypted private channels rather than published where a platform or provider could inspect it. Detection depended instead on a long-running criminal investigation that began in 2023 and moved through messaging groups before reaching the suspect.

What is not established is guilt. The suspect is described as alleged, the case passed to the courts, and a provisional prison order is not a conviction. The reports do not establish which AI tools were used, whether they were commercial or self-hosted, or what role the generated material played in the network's activity.

summary:
Spain's Civil Guard and Morocco's DGST broke up a terrorist network in an operation on July 2, supervised by the National Court. Eight people were arrested in Melilla, Alcobendas, San Sebastián de los Reyes and Málaga, and homes were searched. The investigation began in 2023, targeting young people in Melilla who shared jihadist propaganda in private messaging groups and spread violent ideas, later recruiting others in Madrid and Málaga. The material came from groups such as DAESH and DAESH-KP.

The eight detainees were handed to the courts on July 4, and five were sent to provisional prison. Separately, on July 1, another suspected jihadist was arrested in Cornellá, Barcelona, for using encrypted social media and messaging apps to radicalize others, and for designing jihadist multimedia content with artificial intelligence tools. He was also handed to the courts on July 4 and sent to provisional prison.
